359026.title: Nonexistence of odd-dimensional weakly Hadamard diagonalizable graphs with diagonalizable Laplacians
359026.literal_statement:
A graph $X$ is **weakly Hadamard diagonalizable** if its Laplacian matrix is diagonalized by a weak Hadamard matrix, meaning a matrix with pairwise orthogonal columns whose entries satisfy the weak Hadamard conditions. The Laplacian eigenspaces have equal algebraic and geometric multiplicities when the Laplacian matrix is diagonalizable.

**Odd-dimensional nonexistence conjecture.** For any odd dimension, there is no weakly Hadamard diagonalizable graph whose Laplacian eigenspaces have equal algebraic and geometric multiplicities; equivalently, there is no weak Hadamard matrix with pairwise orthogonal columns diagonalizing the Laplacian matrix of the graph.

This conjecture is motivated by the preceding lemma and corollary concerning weakly Hadamard diagonalizable graphs and their Laplacian eigenspaces. Its resolution would rule out diagonalizable examples in every odd dimension, but the supplied text does not state whether it is known or open.

359157.title: Buck et al.'s three-run enumeration conjecture for flattened 2-Stirling permutations
359157.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{Q}_n$ denote the set of $2$-Stirling permutations of order $n$, and let $\operatorname{flat}_3(\mathcal{Q}_n)$ denote those with exactly three runs. Then $|\operatorname{flat}_3(\mathcal{Q}_n)|$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}
|\operatorname{flat}_3(\mathcal{Q}_n)|={}&2\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\binom{n-1}{i}\left(\sum_{j=2}^{n-1-i}\binom{n-1-i}{j}\right)\\
&+\sum_{i=2}^{n-1}\binom{n-1}{i}\left(\sum_{j=2}^{n-1-i}\binom{n-1-i}{j}\right)+\sum_{i=3}^{n-1}(2^{i-1}-2)\binom{n-1}{i}.
\end{aligned}
$$

**Buck et al.'s three-run enumeration conjecture.** The number of flattened $2$-Stirling permutations of order $n$ with exactly three runs equals the displayed sum.

The formula was conjectured in the cited work and is presented here as a conjecture; the source gives no further resolution status.

359270.title: The cycle double cover conjecture for bridgeless graphs
359270.literal_statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a graph. A **cycle double cover** is a collection of cycles such that every edge of $\Gamma$ lies in exactly two cycles. For a cubic graph, this is equivalent to requiring that exactly three cycles pass through each node. A simplicial surface has $\Gamma$ as its face graph when its faces correspond to the vertices and edges of $\Gamma$ in the usual incidence structure.

**Cycle double cover conjecture.** Every cubic graph containing no bridges has a cycle double cover, or equivalently is the face graph of a simplicial surface. More generally, every bridgeless graph admits a cycle double cover.

The conjecture would characterize which bridgeless cubic graphs arise as face graphs of simplicial surfaces and remains open: it is not known whether all cubic bridgeless graphs admit a cycle double cover.

359362.title: Finite string system conjecture for finitely supported loads
359362.literal_statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a bounded convex domain, and let the load $f \in \mathcal{M}(\overline{\Omega};\mathbb{R})$ be finitely supported. An optimal string system consists of a pair $(\hat\Pi,\hat\pi)$ solving the optimal string system problem. Write $\mathrm{sp}(\hat\Pi,\hat\pi)$ for its support and $\mathrm{sp}\,f$ for the support of the load. **Finite string system conjecture.** A solution of the optimal string system problem exists. Moreover, there is at least one solution $(\hat\Pi,\hat\pi)$ satisfying

$$
\mathrm{sp}(\hat\Pi,\hat\pi) \subset (\partial\Omega \cup \mathrm{sp}\,f) \times (\partial\Omega \cup \mathrm{sp}\,f).
$$

The conjecture predicts that finitely supported loads admit an optimal finite string system whose strings connect only boundary points or points in the support of the load. Its status is not established by the supplied source context.

359750.title: The membrane extension of the sharp cycle bound
359750.literal_statement:
Let $P$ be a minimal membrane of type $A_2$. Write $\operatorname{cyc}(P)$ for the number of cycles in its billiards permutation, $\operatorname{perim}(P)$ for its perimeter, and $\operatorname{comps}(P)$ for its number of components. A membrane is **indecomposable** and **primitive** as in the membrane framework. **The membrane cycle-bound conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{cyc}(P) \leq \frac{1}{4}(\operatorname{perim}(P)+2\operatorname{comps}(P)).
$$

Furthermore, if $P$ is indecomposable, primitive, and not a single edge, then

$$
\operatorname{cyc}(P)=\frac{1}{4}(\operatorname{perim}(P)+2)
$$

if and only if the billiards permutation of $P$ contains exactly two $3$-cycles and no cycles of length greater than $4$. This conjecture extends the corresponding proposed sharp bound from generalized grid polygons to minimal membranes of type $A_2$; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

360138.title: Uniqueness of the adjacent cluster under mutation
360138.literal_statement: Let $(\mathbf x, \mathbf p, B)$ denote a seed in the cluster algebra with coefficients, or let $(\mathbf x,B)$ denote a seed in the coefficient-free cluster algebra. A **cluster** is the set of cluster variables underlying the seed. **Uniqueness of the adjacent cluster under mutation.** Any seed $(\mathbf x, \mathbf p, B)$, or $(\mathbf x,B)$, is uniquely determined by its cluster $\mathbf x$. Thus, for any cluster $\mathbf x$ and any $x\in\mathbf x$, there is a unique cluster $\mathbf x'$ such that $\mathbf x'\cap\mathbf x=\mathbf x\setminus\{x\}$. This asserts that each cluster variable determines a unique neighboring cluster obtained by replacing it, so the exchange graph and cluster complex have the expected mutation structure; the supplied context does not indicate whether the claim is proved or remains open.

360291.title: Existence of minimal uncolorable uniform bi-hypergraphs
360291.literal_statement:
Let $Bi\mathcal{H}yp(n,r)$ be the set of $r$-uniform bi-hypergraphs of order $n$, and let $\mathcal{MUC}(n,r)$ be the set of minimal uncolorable bi-hypergraphs in $Bi\mathcal{H}yp(n,r)$. For $r\ge 3$, every bi-hypergraph in $Bi\mathcal{H}yp(n,r)$ is colorable when $r\le n\le (r-1)^2$, while minimal uncolorable bi-hypergraphs are known to exist at $n=(r-1)^2+1$ in the complete case.

**Existence conjecture.** For any $n,r\in \mathbb{N}$ with $r\ge 3$ and $n\ge (r-1)^2+1$, the set $\mathcal{MUC}(n,r)$ is not empty.

This conjecture concerns the existence of minimal obstructions to proper coloring beyond the first possible uncolorable order and would provide a general response to the existence aspect of the problem posed by Tuza and Voloshin. The supplied text gives no resolution beyond the stated known colorability range.

360957.title: The expansion conjecture for the generating functions $T_{a,k}(x)$
360957.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}_{n,k}^{a\prec n}(1324)$ denote the set of $1324$-avoiding permutations in $\mathcal{S}_n$ whose relevant positional parameters are indexed by $a$ and $k$. Define

$$
T_{a,k}(x)=\sum\limits_{n=k+1}^{\infty}|\mathcal{S}_{n,k}^{a\prec n}(1324)|x^n,
$$

and

$$
g_a(x,t)=\sum\limits_{k=1}^{\infty}t^kT_{a,k}(x).
$$

Let $T_{1,0}(x)=x$ and $T_{a,0}(x)=|\mathcal{S}_{a-1}(1324)|x^a$. Also, let $f(x)$ denote the generating function introduced earlier in the paper. For $k\geq a$, the following formulas are equivalent:

**Expansion conjecture.**

$$
\sum\limits_{j=0}^k(-1)^j\binom{k}{j}f(x)^jT_{a,k-j}(x)=0.
$$

Equivalently,

$$
T_{a,k}(x)=\sum\limits_{j=0}^{a-1}\binom{k}{j}f(x)^{k-j}\sum\limits_{i=0}^{j}(-1)^i\binom{j}{i}f(x)^iT_{a,j-i}(x),
$$

and

$$
T_{a,k}(x)=\sum\limits_{j=0}^{a-1}(-1)^{a-j-1}\binom{k}{j}\binom{k-j-1}{a-j-1}f(x)^{k-j}T_{a,j}(x).
$$

The conjecture proposes an explicit relation between $T_{a,k}(x)$ and powers of $f(x)$ together with the lower-indexed functions $T_{a,j}(x)$. It is motivated by the structural relation between $1324$-avoiding permutations in which entries less than $a$ lie to the right of $n$ and the corresponding reduced permutations, as well as by the proof of the earlier theorem for $T_{2,k}(x)$.

361039.title: Conjectural inversion enumerations for Magog matrices
361039.literal_statement:
Let $\mathrm{Magog}_n$ denote the set of Magog matrices of size $n$, and let $\mathrm{posinv}$ and $\mathrm{inv}$ denote the positive inversion statistic and inversion statistic, respectively. For a statistic $s$, write $|\mathrm{Magog}_n(k~s)|$ for the number of matrices in $\mathrm{Magog}_n$ with statistic $s$ equal to $k$. The conjectured enumerations are:

**Inversion-enumeration conjecture.**

$$
|\mathrm{Magog}_n(1~\mathrm{posinv})|=\binom{n}{2},\qquad n\geq 2,
$$

$$
|\mathrm{Magog}_n(2~\mathrm{posinv})|=2\binom{n-1}{2}+4\binom{n-1}{3}+3\binom{n-1}{4},\qquad n\geq 3,
$$

$$
|\mathrm{Magog}_n(\binom{n}{2}-2~\mathrm{posinv})|=n(n-2),\qquad n\geq 3,
$$

$$
|\mathrm{Magog}_n(\binom{n}{2}-1~\mathrm{inv})|=2^n-n-1,
$$

the $n$th Eulerian number. These formulas are based on numerical data; the second sequence matches OEIS sequence A090809, which counts the coefficient of a certain irreducible character of the symmetric group in a certain Kronecker power. Further verification or proofs of the enumerations remain open.

361121.title: Caterpillar classification conjecture for Penrose caterpillars
361121.literal_statement:
Let $C$ be a Penrose caterpillar, let $S$ be the graded poset of caterpillars used in the source, and let $f_{boat}$ transform a Penrose caterpillar by replacing each relevant subpath along the hull of a boat with the corresponding subpath along the top of the boat. Write $(f_{boat}(C))'$ for its derived path. **Caterpillar classification conjecture.** $C$ belongs to one of the following two sets:

(i) $C$ belongs to the graded poset $S$.

(ii) There exists a caterpillar $C_k$ such that the derived path $(f_{boat}(C))'$ is included in the derived path $(f_{boat}(C_k))'$, up to isomorphism.

The conjecture is intended to describe the possible shapes of fully leafed Penrose trees through the family of Penrose caterpillars and the boat-path transformation. The source states no result resolving this classification.

361271.title: Two-summand criterion for Laurent series over semidomains
361271.literal_statement:
Let $S$ be an **additively reduced and additively atomic semidomain**, and let $cmathcal{A}_{+}(S)$ denote the set of additive atoms of $S$ and $S^{\times}$ its multiplicative unit group. For a Laurent series $f$, write $\operatorname{supp}(f)$ for its support. **Two-summand criterion.** The following statements are equivalent:

1. $\mathcal{A}_{+}(S)=S^{\times}$.
2. Every $f\in S\llbracket x^{\pm1}\rrbracket$ with $|\operatorname{supp}(f)|>1$ can be expressed as the sum of at most two multiplicative irreducibles.
3. There exists $k\in\mathbb{N}$ such that every $f\in S\llbracket x^{\pm1}\rrbracket$ with $|\operatorname{supp}(f)|>1$ can be expressed as the sum of at most $k$ multiplicative irreducibles.

This proposed refinement characterizes exactly when a uniform finite bound on the number of multiplicative irreducible summands improves to the bound two. The source presents it as a conjectural refinement motivated by the established upper bound of three summands; no resolution is supplied.

382247.title: Nonexistence of planar semi-covers of $K_{2,2,2,1}$ under specified conditions
382247.literal_statement: A **planar semi-cover** of $K_{2,2,2,1}$ is a planar graph $G'$ equipped with the projection structure described in the paper. Suppose $G'$ satisfies the following conditions: if $H\subset G'$ is the full preimage of the subgraph $K_4\subset K_{2,2,2,1}$ on vertices $0,-1,-2,-3$, then $H$ is connected, the restriction of the projection map to $H$ is a genuine cover, and the outer boundary $C_e$ of $G'$ is a cycle of $H$; all $3$-cycles of $G'$ are facial; all cycles of the relevant graph $G$ covering the cycles $(1,2,3)$ and $(-1,-2,-3)$ of $K_{2,2,2,1}$ are $3$-cycles; and paths covering other octahedral $3$-cycles may start and end on the boundary of $G'$. **Nonexistence conjecture.** There is no planar semi-cover $G'$ of $K_{2,2,2,1}$ satisfying these conditions. This is presented as a strengthening of the paper's earlier conjecture concerning planar covers, and is intended to eliminate an infinite class of possible components in the proof of the main theorem.

359387.title: Borozenets' rank–crank inequalities modulo 11
359387.literal_statement:
Let $M(m,n)$ and $N(m,n)$ denote, respectively, the numbers of partitions of $n$ with crank and rank $m$. Let $M(a,c;n)$ and $N(a,c;n)$ denote, respectively, the numbers of partitions of $n$ with crank and rank congruent to $a\ \, \left( \mathrm{mod} \, c \right)$. For sequences $a=\{a(n)\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ and $b=\{b(n)\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$, write $a\le_N b$ when $a(n)\le b(n)$ for $n\ge N$, and write $a\le b$ when $a(n)\le b(n)$ for $n\ge0$. For $0\le j,d<11$, define

$$
N_{j,d}(n):=N(j,11;11n+d),\qquad M_{j,d}(n):=M(j,11;11n+d),\qquad p_d(n):=p(11n+d).
$$

**Borozenets' conjecture.** The following chains of inequalities hold:

$$
\begin{aligned}
N_{5,0}&\le N_{4,0}\le_2 N_{3,0}\le M_{1,0}\le \frac{p_0}{11}\le M_{0,0}\le_1 N_{2,0}\le N_{1,0}\le_3 N_{0,0},\\
N_{5,1}&\le N_{4,1}\le N_{3,1}\le_1 M_{0,1}\le M_{2,1}\le \frac{p_1}{11}\le M_{1,1}\le_1 N_{2,1}\le N_{1,1}\le N_{0,1},\\
N_{5,2}&\le N_{4,2}\le N_{3,2}\le M_{0,2}\le \frac{p_2}{11}\le M_{2,2}\le_1 N_{2,2}\le N_{1,2}\le_3 N_{0,2},\\
N_{5,3}&\le N_{4,3}\le N_{3,3}\le M_{1,3}\le \frac{p_3}{11}\le M_{0,3}\le N_{2,3}\le_1 N_{1,3}\le_2 N_{0,3},\\
N_{5,4}&\le_3 N_{4,4}\le N_{3,4}\le_1 M_{1,4}\le \frac{p_4}{11}\le M_{0,4}\le_1 N_{2,4}\le N_{1,4}\le_3 N_{0,4},\\
N_{5,5}&\le N_{4,5}\le_1 N_{3,5}\le M_{2,5}\le \frac{p_5}{11}\le M_{0,5}\le N_{2,5}\le N_{1,5}\le N_{0,5},\\
N_{5,6}&\le_1 N_{4,6}\le N_{3,6}\le \frac{p_6}{11}\le N_{2,6}\le N_{1,6}\le_1 N_{0,6},\\
N_{5,7}&\le N_{4,7}\le N_{3,7}\le M_{0,7}\le \frac{p_7}{11}\le M_{1,7}\le N_{2,7}\le_1 N_{1,7}\le N_{0,7},\\
N_{5,8}&\le N_{4,8}\le N_{3,8}\le M_{0,8}\le_3 \frac{p_8}{11}\le_3 M_{1,8}\le N_{2,8}\le N_{1,8}\le_3 N_{0,8},\\
N_{5,9}&\le N_{4,9}\le N_{3,9}\le_1 M_{0,9}\le \frac{p_9}{11}\le M_{1,9}\le N_{2,9}\le N_{1,9}\le_2 N_{0,9},\\
N_{5,10}&\le N_{4,10}\le N_{3,10}\le_1 M_{3,10}\le \frac{p_{10}}{11}\le M_{0,10}\le N_{2,10}\le N_{1,10}\le_3 N_{0,10}.
\end{aligned}
$$

These inequalities were conjectured by Borozenets and are the subject of the paper's proofs; the supplied source does not explicitly provide a resolution status for this statement.

364307.title: Hameed's conjecture on semi-transitivity of Mycielski graphs
364307.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\mu(G)$ denote its Mycielski graph. A graph is **semi-transitive** if it admits an acyclic orientation with no shortcut. **Hameed's conjecture.** For every graph $G$, the graph $\mu(G)$ is semi-transitive if and only if $G$ is a bipartite graph. Hameed proved this equivalence when $G$ is a comparability graph, while the assertion for arbitrary graphs remains open.

372783.title: The graph-product conjecture for linear sofic groups
372783.literal_statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be a field, let $V$ be a set, and let $\lbrace \Gamma_v: v \in V \rbrace$ be a family of $\mathbb{K}$-linear sofic groups. For a graph $X=(V,E)$, write

$$
G_X=\left(\ast_{v\in V}\Gamma_v\right)/\ll h^{-1}k^{-1}hk:(v,w)\in E,\ h\in\Gamma_v,\ k\in\Gamma_w\gg.
$$

**The graph-product conjecture.** The free product $\ast_{v\in V}\Gamma_v$ is $\mathbb{K}$-linear sofic, and, more generally, $G_X$ is $\mathbb{K}$-linear sofic for every graph $X=(V,E)$ on $V$.

The paper states that closure under direct sums is known, while closure under free products is claimed in the literature with a gap in the proof; the conjecture would establish permanence of $\mathbb{K}$-linear soficity under all graph products.

373538.title: The corona–kernel bound for graphs with odd cycles
373538.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $\textnormal{corona}(G)$ for its corona, $\textnormal{ker}(G)$ for its kernel, and let $\alpha(G)$ denote its independence number. Let $k$ be the number of odd cycles in $G$.

**Corona–kernel conjecture.** For every graph $G$,

$$
\left|\textnormal{corona}(G)\right|+\left|\textnormal{ker}(G)\right|\le 2\alpha(G)+k.
$$

This conjecture extends the corresponding equality and inequality phenomena for corona and core in König–Egerváry graphs and general graphs. Its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.

375393.title: Havet–Horsch–Rambaud lexicographic-product conjecture for inversion diameter
375393.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $t$ be a positive integer. Denote by $G[\overline{K_t}]$ the lexicographic product obtained by replacing each vertex of $G$ with an independent set of size $t$, and write $I(G)$ for the inversion graph and $\operatorname{diam}(I(G))$ for its diameter.

**Havet–Horsch–Rambaud's lexicographic-product conjecture.** For every graph $G$ and every positive integer $t$,

$$
\operatorname{diam}(I(G[\overline{K_t}]))\le t\cdot\operatorname{diam}(I(G)).
$$

The conjecture predicts that lexicographic blow-ups by independent sets increase inversion diameter by at most the blow-up factor. It is presented as a proposed general bound, and no resolution is supplied in the source.

375796.title: The affine upper-bound conjecture for sequential cable width
375796.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\mathrm{lrw}(G)$ denote its linear rank-width, and let $\mathrm{lsfw}(G)$ denote its sequential cable width. **Affine upper-bound conjecture.** For every graph $G$, 

$$
\mathrm{lsfw}(G)\le 2\,\mathrm{lrw}(G)+2.
$$

The preceding results establish the corresponding lower bound and settle the level-one case, while the upper bound remains open beyond level one. The conjecture proposes an affine calibration between sequential cable width and linear rank-width.
